articles.summary: Sony researchers describe how TQT uses the straight-through estimator to learn the quantizer's dynamic range by gradient descent (p. 2) and cite it for the power-of-two step size that efficient hardware requires (p. 4). They train a TQT model, learning qmax at a fixed bitwidth "as was done in (Jain et al., 2019)", as the fixed-bitwidth benchmark for their concurrently developed mixed-precision method, and report the TQT rows in their CIFAR-10 and ImageNet result tables (pp. 8–9).

articles.summary: NVIDIA and Bilkent University researchers adopt TQT as the baseline quantized retraining method for their study of orthogonality regularization, describing it as achieving state-of-the-art results (pp. 1–2). They state "we use TQT [25] as our baseline retraining" (p. 5), train thresholds in the log domain as described in [25] (p. 4), follow its five-epoch retraining schedule (p. 5) and combine the orthogonality penalty with TQT, reporting results with and without TQT in Section V-A (p. 6).

articles.summary: The Bayesian Bits authors credit two papers, LSQ [8] and reference [15], the TQT work by Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick, with independently introducing joint learning of the quantization scale and network parameters for a fixed-bitwidth network (p. 6). Figure 2b then compares Bayesian Bits on MobileNetV2 with AdaRound, LSQ and TQT (p. 8).

articles.summary: University of California, Santa Cruz and Intel researchers explain that Jain et al. and Esser et al. showed quantization thresholds could be trained, with a straight-through-estimator gradient that lets thresholds grow for dynamic range or shrink for precision (p. 3). For the quantization of their 4-bit QW-Net image-reconstruction network they state "Following Jain et al. [2019], we train the thresholds in log space" to improve stability during quantized training (Section 5.1, p. 6).

articles.summary: ETH Zürich and University of Bologna researchers train their ternarized gesture-recognition networks with two quantization-aware training algorithms, INQ and TQT. They describe TQT as optimizing the logarithm of the clipping interval (p. 5), use it to learn both weight and activation clipping bounds (p. 6), list its hyperparameters (p. 9) and compare it with INQ in Table 4, where ReLU activations with TQT give the highest classification accuracy (p. 10).

(p. 3), and adapt this jointly credited procedure to learn weight and activation ranges for BERT-like transformer models in their quantization-aware training variant (p. 7).

articles.summary: Snap Inc., Northeastern University and Rice University researchers position F8Net against the fixed-point quantization of Jain et al. (2019), which uses trainable power-of-two scale factors so that multiplication becomes bit shifting, and state that their work differs from it in three major aspects (pp. 2–3). They contrast F8Net's on-the-fly fractional length with TQT's directly trained fractional length (p. 7) and list TQT (Jain et al., 2019) in Table 1 for MobileNet V1 and V2b as the previous fixed-point quantization method (p. 8).

articles.summary: Xilinx researchers in Beijing re-implement a hardware-friendly quantization baseline following references [19, 21], where [19] is TQT: power-of-two step sizes, low-bit first and last layers, quantized inputs and outputs of element-wise additions, 8-bit biases and batch normalization merged during training. They build bin regularization on this TQT baseline; Table 9 reports 63.8% top-1 for TQT, 65.8% for TQT+L2 and 67.5% for TQT+BR on 4-bit MobileNetV2, which the text describes as +3.7% over TQT (p. 8). Employer-linked: the authors list Xilinx Inc.

articles.summary: Inha University and Sangmyung University researchers build log level threshold quantization (LLTQ) on TQT's power-of-two scale mapping, where a trainable log-threshold turns scale multiplication into shifts (p. 6). LLTQ maps the trainable parameter directly to a power-of-two scale and initializes activation scales from first-batch statistics in place of TQT's pre-calibration. They illustrate LSQ, TQT and LLTQ (Figure 3, p. 7), train all three (p. 10) and report TQT as hardware-friendly within about 0.45% of floating-point accuracy, a gap LLTQ closes (p. 11).
articles.authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

articles.summary: KU Leuven researchers adopt TQT's quantizer: they optimize power-of-two scales by backpropagation "as proposed by Jain et al." (p. 12) and quantize activations with its symmetric uniform quantizer, hyperparameters and scale freezing (p. 17). They credit Jain et al. with showing that 8-bit models with power-of-two scales reach full-precision accuracy (p. 14), discuss TQT's shared elementwise-addition quantizer parameters (p. 12), extend its gradual freezing and stabilization criteria to per-channel scales (p. 19) and report TQT on ImageNet (Table 2, p. 20).

TQT is applied together with activation and training refinements, so the reported results reflect the combined pipeline.

articles.summary: Seoul National University and Qualcomm researchers describe LSQ [8] and TQT [17] as introducing uniform quantization with trainable interval values and state that QKD leverages these trainable approaches in its baseline quantization implementation (p. 2), with trainable interval parameters for each layer's weights and input activations similar to [8, 17, 45] (p. 3). They also cite TQT on the quantization sensitivity of depthwise convolutions (p. 7). Knowledge distillation is applied on top of this quantization baseline, and the reported results cover the combined method.

It also cites Jain et al. among works that start quantization-aware training from a pretrained FP32 model (p. 22).

articles.summary: Kyushu Institute of Technology researchers build ITBWN by quantizing activations to INT8 with TQT while using binary or ternary weights, describing TQT's power-of-two scale, removal of the zero point and threshold training with the straight-through estimator (p. 2). TQT quantizes the activations in their binary, ternary and INT8 configurations (pp. 3–4) through the Xilinx Brevitas implementation, whose default settings, as the authors note, omit the power-of-two scale constraint and initialize the scale differently (p. 3).

articles.summary: The Alan Turing Institute researchers deploy a YOLOv8-based SAR vessel detector on an AMD/Xilinx Kria KV260 FPGA, quantizing it to INT8 with the Vitis AI Quantizer using symmetric power-of-two scaling and quantization-aware training with a straight-through estimator, for which they cite TQT [35] (p. 5). They retrain with a tuned quantizer-parameter learning rate and report that the deployed QAT models match the expected GPU performance with little to no degradation (Table 4, Section 4.3, p. 11). TQT is cited by reference number rather than named, and is applied through the AMD/Xilinx Vitis AI toolchain.
